text: {"features":[{"name":"Role-specific motivation","description":"How specifically and convincingly the letter explains why this exact Information Security Engineering role at Google fits the applicant's goals.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Uses a formulaic statement of interest and mostly restates that the applicant meets requirements."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Gives a general reason for applying, such as security impact or Google scale, but the rationale could fit many other roles."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Connects interest to one specific aspect of the posting, such as secure defaults, automation, or foundational systems."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Ties several specific elements of the role or team to the applicant's prior work or stated career direction."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Makes the application feel deliberately chosen by weaving multiple details of the posting into a clear next-step narrative."}]},{"name":"Security automation mandate","description":"How well the letter shows understanding that the job is about scaling security work through centralized automation and tooling.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Refers to security or tooling in broad terms without clearly showing that the role centers on automating security workflows at scale."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Acknowledges that automation matters but describes it only at a high level and without much sense of the underlying security processes."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Clearly recognizes that the role reduces manual security effort through tooling, triage, or secure-by-default systems."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows concrete understanding of how centralized tools can scale scarce security expertise across teams and the development lifecycle."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Demonstrates nuanced grasp of the mandate by discussing several role-relevant mechanisms such as triage, variant analysis, risk reduction, and developer guidance."}]},{"name":"Security collaboration orientation","description":"How strongly the letter signals readiness to work closely with security engineers and adjacent stakeholders rather than treating the role as purely solo implementation.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Says little or nothing about working with security engineers or the teams who would rely on the tools."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Uses generic teamwork language but does not explain how collaboration would matter in this role."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Indicates willingness to partner with security or product teams as part of the job."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Explicitly frames the work as collaborating with security specialists or building tools in service of other teams."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Treats partnership as central, showing that the goal is to amplify security experts through close technical collaboration and usable systems."}]},{"name":"Platform mindset","description":"How strongly the letter shows interest in building foundational systems whose impact scales across many teams or products.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Gives little sign of wanting to build shared systems with broad downstream impact."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions scale or impact in passing but not specifically as a platform or infrastructure concern."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows clear interest in foundational tooling or systems that benefit many teams."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Explicitly frames the work in terms of central infrastructure, inherited improvements, or organization-wide leverage."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Makes platform leverage a defining theme by describing success as multiplying capacity or improving defaults across a large engineering surface."}]},{"name":"Developer enablement orientation","description":"How strongly the letter treats security engineering as enabling product teams through usable defaults and low-friction tooling.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Does not address how security tooling should serve the developers who use it."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Suggests interest in security outcomes without discussing developer experience or workflow friction."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Recognizes that good security systems should reduce manual effort or make safer behavior easier."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Explicitly emphasizes helping busy engineers follow secure practices through low-friction tooling or defaults."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Makes developer enablement central, portraying the best security engineering as quietly helping other teams do the right thing by default."}]},{"name":"Software delivery track record","description":"How convincingly the letter establishes sustained experience testing, maintaining, and launching production software.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Establishes only baseline professional depth, such as a few years of experience and limited scope of launched services."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Shows credible production experience but with modest breadth or ownership."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Presents solid mid-level delivery experience across multiple production services over several years."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows strong lifecycle ownership through longer tenure, repeated launches, and clear responsibility for testing, maintenance, and release."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Conveys extensive and sustained production depth with repeated service launches and a strong sense of end-to-end software ownership."}]},{"name":"Go backend fit","description":"How strongly the letter establishes Go as a core language for backend systems relevant to the role.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Names Go as part of the background but does not make it sound central to recent professional work."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Describes professional Go use but with limited evidence of backend ownership or depth."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Makes clear that Go is a regular language used in production service development."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Presents Go as a primary or daily language and ties it to substantial backend or infrastructure work."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows especially strong alignment by centering recent backend accomplishments in Go and making the language feel directly transferable to the role."}]},{"name":"Python fit","description":"How strongly the letter establishes Python capability relevant to automation, tooling, or agents.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Gives no meaningful evidence of Python use or mentions it only indirectly."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions Python briefly without showing that it mattered to real systems or automation."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Describes regular Python use for tooling, scripting, services, or analysis."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows strong Python experience in production tooling or services that other engineers depend on."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Positions Python as a major strength, especially for robust automation layers, internal services, or agent implementations."}]},{"name":"Algorithmic fluency","description":"How convincingly the letter demonstrates practical strength with data structures and algorithms.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no concrete evidence of strength with data structures and algorithms."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Claims algorithmic ability in general terms but without a specific example."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Supports the claim with one clear example of improving a real system through better structure or algorithm choice."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Uses a concrete example to show strong practical fluency on a performance, matching, scheduling, deduplication, or similar problem."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Makes the algorithmic case especially compelling by showing how deliberate design turned a hard or bottlenecked problem into a tractable one."}]},{"name":"AI production experience","description":"How well the letter shows experience building and operating AI-enabled features in production settings.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Does not mention any AI-related work."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"References AI only as interest or light exposure rather than real delivery."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Describes shipping model-backed or LLM-based functionality in production."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Adds operational maturity by discussing evaluation, trust, guardrails, or failure handling."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows especially strong AI readiness by pairing production delivery with explicit attention to reliability, evaluation, and responsible deployment."}]},{"name":"Agentic systems design","description":"How strongly the letter establishes experience designing agent-style systems with bounded actions and supporting infrastructure.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Does not mention agent-style systems or uses the term without describing actual design work."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions agentic tooling but leaves the architecture or constraints unclear."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Describes building agent-based systems with a recognizable split between agents and supporting services."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Explains a credible design in which Python agents act within boundaries enforced, logged, or supervised by backend systems."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Gives a strong role-matched picture of agentic design, including constraints, permissions, auditing, or explicit supervision of agent behavior."}]},{"name":"Vulnerability workflow automation","description":"How directly the letter shows experience automating vulnerability handling or report triage.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Does not show direct experience automating vulnerability handling or triage."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Refers to reducing security toil or improving workflows but not to a specific vulnerability-report process."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Clearly states that the applicant automated vulnerability report triage, routing, or handling."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Adds concrete workflow detail, such as classification, queue reduction, or routing logic."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Makes the relevance especially strong by explaining the operational effect, such as materially reducing manual handling or returning expert time to the team."}]},{"name":"Security assessment experience","description":"How convincingly the letter demonstrates hands-on experience reviewing systems for security weaknesses.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no clear evidence of having performed security assessments."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Implies some security awareness but not actual review or assessment work."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"States experience with security reviews, threat modeling, code review, or assessments in a believable way."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Describes assessments with concrete scope, such as new designs, legacy services, or multiple system layers."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Conveys strong practitioner depth by explaining the assessment mindset, the types of findings pursued, or follow-through to remediation."}]},{"name":"Offensive security grounding","description":"How much the letter shows practical attacker-oriented security grounding through certifications, competitions, or equivalent practice.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Offers no attacker-oriented evidence beyond general security interest."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Shows light grounding through a baseline certification or occasional competition participation."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Demonstrates meaningful attacker orientation through regular CTF practice, attacker-framed experience, or a recognized certification."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows strong offensive grounding through high CTF performance or a demanding hands-on certification such as OSCP."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Combines substantial practice with strong external validation, making offensive security skills feel especially credible."}]},{"name":"Technical initiative beyond assigned work","description":"How strongly the letter shows self-directed engineering initiative outside ordinary job duties.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Gives little evidence of self-directed technical work outside normal job duties."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions a small side project or occasional external contribution without showing sustained effort."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows clear initiative through a maintained project, useful tool, or intermittent upstream contribution."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Demonstrates strong initiative through either a substantial personal system build or stewardship of an actively used open-source project."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows exceptional initiative through sustained ownership of ambitious systems or community-used open-source work that required real design, review, and release discipline."}]},{"name":"Specificity of evidence","description":"How concrete the letter's claims are about past work rather than generic self-description.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Relies mostly on broad self-descriptions and abstract claims."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Includes a few named technologies or tasks but leaves many claims generic."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Regularly grounds claims in concrete systems, workflows, or engineering problems."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Uses multiple specific, technically credible examples that make the experience easy to picture."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Consistently turns claims into evidence with precise, role-relevant examples throughout the letter."}]},{"name":"Impact articulation","description":"How clearly the letter explains the results or value of the applicant's work.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Describes activities performed but rarely explains what changed because of them."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Hints at positive results in broad terms without making the effect very tangible."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Connects some examples to clear benefits such as less manual work, better performance, or improved reliability."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Repeatedly ties work to meaningful team or system impact, such as reclaimed capacity, simplified operations, or wider reuse."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Makes impact vivid and convincing by showing how the work changed team capacity, system behavior, or organizational leverage."}]},{"name":"Fit argument coherence","description":"How well the letter is organized into a clear, persuasive case that the applicant matches the role.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Reads mainly as a disconnected list of qualifications."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Has a basic structure but the case for fit feels only partly integrated."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Presents a coherent case with a recognizable theme and supporting evidence."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Maintains a strong through-line that repeatedly connects experience back to the role."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Delivers a tightly organized argument in which nearly every paragraph advances the same clear case for fit."}]},{"name":"Writing mechanics","description":"How polished the prose is in spelling, grammar, and proofreading.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Contains frequent errors that noticeably distract from meaning or professionalism."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Has recurring typos or mechanical issues that a reader will repeatedly notice."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Has some minor errors but remains easy to read."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Is mostly clean, with only occasional small mistakes."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Is essentially error-free and clearly proofread."}]}]}
